svg.text: PR #1909: replace an unused smaller lcore table in mtl_init — states tested on the host table
Two builds of the PR: RTE_MAX_LCORE 128 (table 22532 B, /usr/local DPDK) and 256 (table 45060 B). Probe = mtl_init + mtl_start on kernel:lo, as root. Key 0x15050005.
State before mtl_init
What the PR did
Result

g.text: 128 build SIGKILLed: 22532 B table, nattch 0, stale entry. Then a 256 build.
removed it, made the 45060 B table, took lcore 1
refused "in use, nattch 1"; the live table and its entry stay
256 build SIGKILLed: 45060 B table, nattch 0. Then a 128 build, then a 256 build.
nothing to replace; the 128 build uses the first 128 entries
both on one table, lcore 1 and lcore 2
128 stale table. Two 256 builds call mtl_init at the same time.
the lock file orders them: one replaces, the other attaches; lcore 1 and 2
128 stale table of root. A 256 build as a user that is not root.
"can not remove ..., Operation not permitted"; the table stays
128 stale table, MtlManager up. A 256 build.
connects to MtlManager, does not touch the table
128 stale table, MtlManager stopped. A 256 build.
removed it, made the 45060 B table
128 stale table; LcoreMgr --info (128) holds it 1 s for its CPU sample. A 256 build.
refused "in use, nattch 1": mtl_init fails, LcoreMgr then removes the table

svg.text: Unit: the 3 MtSchLcoreShm cases of the PR pass, the full suite passes (2077). PR CI: 33 pass, 11 skipped. No fault found in the change of the PR.
Older faults next to it (not from this PR)
1. MtlManager and the shm table are two lcore maps: one CPU goes to two processes
MtlManager map
lcores of connected processes
shm table, key 0x15050005
lcores of single instance mode
CPU 1
two busy-polls
P1
P2
H2: P1 has lcore 1 from MtlManager; MtlManager is SIGKILLed; P2 starts
P1 sch_get_lcore, succ on manager lcore 1
P2 mt_instance_init, connect to manager fail, assume single instance mode
P2 sch_get_lcore, succ on shm lcore 1
H3: P1 has lcore 1 from the shm table; MtlManager starts; P2 starts
P1 sch_get_lcore, succ on shm lcore 1
P2 sch_get_lcore, succ on manager lcore 1
Each map does not know the other. doc/shm_lcore.md does not tell to not mix the two modes.
2. LcoreMgr --clean_pid_auto_check logs the delete, but the entry stays active
before: lcore 1 active pid 2721803 (live) lcore 2 active pid 2722089 (SIGKILLed) used 2 nattch 1
tool: lcore_shm_clean_auto_pid, delete dead lcore 2 from the shared mem, PID 2722089
after: lcore 1 active pid 2721803 lcore 2 active pid 2722089 used 2
lcore_shm_clean_auto_pid() only counts: no "shm_entry->active = false", no "used--". Unit test: MtSchLcoreShm.AutoCleanFreesTheEntryOfADeadPid (fails).
3. Smaller LcoreMgr faults
- LcoreMgr exits 0 when sch_lcore_shm_init() fails (a 256 build on a 128 table: "Invalid argument", rc 0).
- LcoreMgr --info and the clean actions remove a table with no process attached as they exit (the last-user rule of sch_lcore_shm_uinit()),
and they attach with no lock file. L2 above is that window.
Branch with the probe results and the failing test: DawidWesierski4:pr-1909-review (PR head afc4cc6b + 1 test commit).
Run 2026-11-23 on the dev host (256 CPUs, 2 NUMA nodes), MtlManager of the same tree, no other MTL process.
